ruling:
## The Ruling

The letter as submitted is a verdict dressed as an inspection. Ray stood on the shingles, read the gutters, counted the years, and sold a tear-off — the besetting sin is **never-price-off-the-roof-surface**, and it drags four more behind it: **roof-age-alone-never-justifies-replacement**, **granules-alone-never-justify-replacement**, **paired-moisture-reading-on-stained-vs-clean-shea**, and **flash-photo-the-deck-from-inside**. Then, having built a replacement on nothing, he offered to make the insurer's paperwork "read the way it needs to read," which is **never-write-a-wind-event-as-a-storm-replacement** broken in the plainest words I have seen.

The Editor's correction is **accepted with the amendments below**. The Editor cut the verdict and the insurance paragraph cleanly and installed the attic protocol in the right place. But the Editor stopped at the pricing paragraph and left the back half of the letter still selling a job that no longer exists on the page.

## The Audit Reckoned

**Pricing Decisions sheet**

- **never-write-a-wind-event-as-a-storm-replacement — Sustained.** The evidence is exact. The Editor deleted the paragraph outright rather than rewording it; that is the correct fix. There is no factual-findings version of "send him to me and I will make sure it reads the way it needs to read."
- **roof-age-alone-never-justifies-replacement — Sustained.** The Editor kept the facts (1999 house, original shingles, twenty-seven years) and struck the conclusion. Correct. Age is a fact to record, not a diagnosis to bill.
- **granules-alone-never-justify-replacement — Sustained.** "The gutters tell me everything" is the sentence this rule was written against. The Editor's replacement is sound.
- **within-two-points…, 3-6-point-spread…, 6-point-spread… — Not applicable, sustained as to the main roof, but overruled as to the low-slope section.** The auditor was literal: no readings were taken, so no spread exists to apply. But the text pre-decides the outcome those three rules exist to decide. "I can shingle-patch that one while we are up there at no extra charge rather than doing the membrane, which would add a few thousand" is a remedy and a price for a slope with a known leak, chosen from the surface with no reading on its sheathing. The Editor left it standing untouched. **Amendment ordered:** strike that sentence and replace with: *"I also noticed the low-slope section over the family room addition is leaking. That section gets its own paired readings on the sheathing below it, and the remedy for that slope follows the spread — I will not choose between a patch and a membrane until I have the numbers."* Rule ids: **never-price-off-the-roof-surface** (a remedy and a "no extra charge" price quoted from the surface), with **3-6-point-spread-slope-repair-with-deck-allowanc** and **6-point-spread-tear-off-that-slope** as the rules that will actually decide it.
- **wind-event-priced-by-course-not-by-square-plus-r — Not applicable, sustained.** No wind repair was scoped; the wind was used as an insurance lever, not as a course count.

**Attic & Moisture Diagnosis sheet**

- **never-price-off-the-roof-surface — Sustained, and the Editor's fix is incomplete.** The $18,450 was removed and replaced with a commitment to quote after attic, meter, and flash photo. Good. But two sentences later the letter still says: *"We have a crew free Thursday and I am holding that slot for you until tomorrow afternoon. If you can sign today I can lock in this price before the October material increase."* There is no price in the letter to lock. Worse, "sign today" asks the Alvarados to commit to work that has not been diagnosed — that is pricing off the surface with the number hidden instead of shown. **Amendment ordered:** strike both sentences. Replace with: *"I would like to come back and get into the attic this week. Once I have the readings and the deck photos, you will have my findings and a quote, and you can take your time with both."* Rule id: **never-price-off-the-roof-surface**.
- **paired-moisture-reading-on-stained-vs-clean-shea — Sustained.** The Editor wrote "paired pin moisture meter readings on the sheathing." Acceptable, but the rule specifies the three points: top of the stain, 18 inches upslope, clean sheathing on the same slope. A homeowner who is told the method can hold the roofer to it. **Amendment ordered:** revise to *"take pin moisture readings on the sheathing at the top of the stain, eighteen inches upslope of it, and on clean sheathing on the same slope."*
- **flash-photo-the-deck-from-inside — Sustained.** Editor's fix is correct and sufficient.
- **deck-photo-overrides-the-meter, chimney-within-six-feet, every-flashing-repair-leaves-with-three-document, no-stain-attic-check, daylight-at-ridge, daylight-at-penetration — Not applicable, all sustained.** No chimney location is given relative to the stain, no daylight is reported, no flashing repair has been scoped. I will not invent findings the text does not contain.

**One further residue the auditors did not flag:** *"My work is warrantied for ten years, and that covers the whole roof, including the chimney and the gutters."* A whole-roof warranty presumes a whole-roof job, and the letter no longer scopes one. This is the tear-off verdict surviving in the closing line. **Amendment ordered** under **never-price-off-the-roof-surface**: revise to *"Whatever the findings call for, my work carries a ten-year warranty, and the scope of that warranty will be spelled out in the quote."*

Nothing sound was "fixed" by the Editor; every edit in the ledger stands.

## Conflicts With Common Practice

1. **never-price-off-the-roof-surface.** Convention: a roofer who walks the roof gives the homeowner a number before he leaves the driveway; making them wait looks indecisive. My way stands because the deck is what you are replacing, and you have not seen it. A number given before the attic is a guess with a dollar sign.
2. **roof-age-alone-never-justifies-replacement.** Convention: twenty-seven years on a twenty-five-year shingle is a dead roof, full stop. My way stands because the shingle's rated life is a warranty term, not a moisture reading. Plenty of twenty-seven-year decks meter dry.
3. **granules-alone-never-justify-replacement.** Convention: granules in the gutter are "the classic sign." My way stands because granules are wear, not water. Water shows up in the sheathing or it does not.
4. **never-write-a-wind-event-as-a-storm-replacement.** Convention treats steering a claim as doing the homeowner a favor — "a new roof on their dollar." My way stands because the scope goes to the adjuster as what was found, in the words the findings support. Nothing else.
5. **Hold-the-slot, sign-today, beat-the-price-increase.** Convention calls this closing. Under **never-price-off-the-roof-surface** it is asking for a signature on an undiagnosed roof, and it goes.
6. **The free shingle patch on the low slope.** Convention says throw the homeowner a bone while the crew is up there. Under the spread rules, the remedy for that slope is decided by its own readings, not by what is convenient Thursday.

## The Lesson

1. **Habit: diagnosing from the gutter and the driveway.** "I did not need to go into the attic to know what that means — after nineteen years in this trade, the gutters tell me everything." Forbidden by **never-price-off-the-roof-surface** and **flash-photo-the-deck-from-inside**. Rewritten: *"I found a soft spot near the bathroom vent and granules in the gutters. Neither tells me the condition of the deck. I need to get into the attic with the meter and a flash before I tell you what this roof needs."*

2. **Habit: letting the calendar and the shingle age pronounce the verdict.** "We are twenty-seven years into a twenty-five year roof. At that age there is no repair worth your money." Forbidden by **roof-age-alone-never-justifies-replacement** and **granules-alone-never-justify-replacement**. Rewritten: *"It is a 1999 house on the original shingles, so we are twenty-seven years into a twenty-five-year roof. That tells me to look hard. It does not tell me what I will find."*

3. **Habit: writing the paper for the payer instead of from the roof.** "If your adjuster wants a scope, send him to me and I will make sure it reads the way it needs to read." Forbidden by **never-write-a-wind-event-as-a-storm-replacement**. Rewritten: *"If you choose to involve your insurer, I will give the adjuster the same findings I give you — readings, photos, and what they show — and nothing beyond that."*

## The Verdict on the Text

The Editor's corrected text **does not yet pass**. It removes the verdict, the insurance steering, and the surface price, but it leaves the letter asking for a signature today on a price it no longer states, pre-scopes a free shingle patch on an unread low slope, and warranties a whole roof it has not scoped. **It passes once the amendments above are applied.** The final corrected text in full:

> **Subject: Your roof — recommendation and price**
>
> Dear Mr. and Mrs. Alvarado,
>
> Thanks for having me out this morning. I walked the roof and conducted an initial assessment. It is a 1999 house and you are on the original shingles, so we are twenty-seven years into a twenty-five-year roof. That tells me to look hard. It does not tell me what I will find. To determine whether repair or replacement is appropriate, I will need to inspect the attic, decking, and moisture levels.
>
> I found a soft spot near the bathroom vent and the gutters have granule accumulation. Before determining the next steps, I need to get into the attic to take pin moisture readings on the sheathing at the top of the stain, eighteen inches upslope of it, and on clean sheathing on the same slope; photograph the underside of the roof deck from inside with the flash on; and evaluate for actual water penetration. This will properly diagnose what is causing your ceiling stain in the back bedroom.
>
> Following the complete attic inspection, moisture readings, and deck photography, I will provide the factual physical findings and a formal quote based on the deck condition.
>
> I also noticed the low-slope section over the family room addition is leaking. That section gets its own paired readings on the sheathing below it, and the remedy for that slope follows the spread — I will not choose between a patch and a membrane until I have the numbers.
>
> I would like to come back and get into the attic this week. Once I have the readings and the deck photos, you will have my findings and a quote, and you can take your time with both.
>
> Whatever the findings call for, my work carries a ten-year warranty, and the scope of that warranty will be spelled out in the quote.
>
> Warm regards,
> Ray Mensing
> Mensing Exteriors
